- Time sync / NTP: Ensure at least two internal NTP servers reachable from the enclave. (Owner: Solstice)
- Audit logs & access: We'll need at least 30 days of audit logs from the private control plane for our SOC audit — confirm retention or arrange export. (Owner: Redwood ops / Solstice compliance)

Stephanie / team — quick notes from a runtime/connectivity perspective:

1) VPC peering / routing: We support either model but strongly prefer a managed egress tunnel into a Redwood-managed egress subnet (simpler routing for multi-tenant egress). If customer prefers transit VPC, we'll need a route table that directs 10.20.0.0/16 -> Redwood transit. ETA: config snippets by 7/6.

2) Egress IPs: We'll provide a short list of 3 static /29 ranges for production; for staging we can use the same but note different NAT configs. ETA: list by 7/6 (Ben).

3) KMS: Minimal metadata: key ARN, key policy document, and whether key is multi-region. HSM: only if customer requires FIPS/HSM-backed CMKs; Redwood supports AWS KMS & customer-managed CloudHSM. ETA: guidance doc 7/6.

4) Proxy/TLS interception: Ask customer to run: curl -v -x http://<proxy>:8080 https://example.com and provide the proxy cert chain. If interception present, we need the CA bundle to install in our runtime image. Also provide an example host for outbound SNI testing. ETA: test snippet added to response 7/6.

5) Bastion / session recording: We require a jumpbox public IP (or private access via vpn) and whether Solstice will forward session logs. If they want forwarding, we can accept S3 ingestion or syslog — provide format. ETA: options by 7/6.

6) MTU: Runtime tolerates fragmentation but KV-cache latency spikes have been observed with >1500 MTU on tunnels; recommend 1500 unless performance tests show otherwise. Note this in the gap list.

7) DNS: Recommend private hosted zone delegation into the Solstice VPC for the model endpoints — conditional forwarder increases complexity. We'll document the zone delegation steps. ETA: doc 7/6.

8) NTP: Allow UDP/123 to two internal NTP servers; recommend stratum-1/2 with fallback to public NTP in emergencies.

9) Audit logs: We can export control-plane audit logs to a customer S3 bucket or forward to a Splunk/Datadog endpoint. Default retention is 30 days; archival to S3 available. ETA: export playbook by 7/8.

I'll assemble the config snippets and push into the RedWood prereq doc and share back.

—Ben
